title: a build that removes a charter repoints the tickets it owns
intention: A build that deletes or renames an intention+why.json while any ticket's owning_intention still names that path is red at its crossing. The sieve names the ticket, the path and the commit. It goes green when those tickets are repointed in the same change, or when the build's own ticket carries a valid forwarding order for the path. A build that touches no charter adds no finding. A git read failure is red as a failure to read, never clean.
why: Measured 2026-11-14, from the census in ticket A. Two cases are the reason this tooth exists. (1) f942a413f26d (60e1dd170, 2026-11-13) moved the inference proxy's charter. Git records a delete plus an add, not a rename, and f942's plan carries no forwarding order, so 25 tickets were left naming cairn/devices/inference_domain/intention+why.json and build_inspector's successor door answers none of them. (2) The 11-08 retirements deleted six charters that 13 tickets still name: counting_block and post_commit by 6935a4a71f93 (f2b0d8105), ruling by 640a7a48e1c5 (95ae4ef7a), cairnmap by d547b4859f9a (3882dac1c), liveness by 6208d0a27d6e (b514f6a5f), and hermes before this repo's history. Every one of those crossings was green. ticket_inspector.owning_intention_resolves sees the dead owners, but it runs only inside an advisory watch probe, so nothing at the crossing ever read them.
traces_to: Law 4 (a rule that matters is physics: 'a move repoints its owners' was policy and was broken twice in a week), Law 7 (a dead pointer in a record of truth is an error that looks like data), Law 5.

clauses.claim: THE f942 CASE: in a scratch cairn repo plus commons, a commit that deletes devices/x/intention+why.json and adds devices/y/intention+why.json with different enough content that git records D plus A, not R, while a scratch ticket's owning_intention names the old path, is red at the sieve. The finding names the ticket id, the old path and the commit

THE 11-08 CASE: a commit that only deletes a charter some ticket names (a retirement) is red the same way. It is green when that ticket's owning_intention is rewritten in the same commit range to 'none because <path> was retired by ticket <id> ...' or to an existing charter
a forwarding order on the crossing ticket that validly forwards the old path (_valid_orders: from gone, to standing) clears the finding. An order whose 'to' does not exist does not clear it
a commit range that deletes or renames no intention+why.json adds no finding. When git cannot be read, the sieve returns a finding of its own named for the failure to read, never []

decisions.text: D1 THE SIEVE: a sieve, charter_removal_repoints_its_owners, registered among build_inspector's crossing sieves. It reads the crossing build's commit range with git diff --name-status (D and R entries) for intention+why.json paths. For each one, it reds every plan whose owning_intention still names the old path, unless that ticket's own plan was changed in the same range or the crossing ticket's forwarding order validly forwards the path (_valid_orders: from gone, to standing). The red names the ticket, the path and the commit. On a git read failure it reds as a failure to read, never as clean.
D2 ONE PROOF, red first, one tooth per clause, each in a scratch git repo plus commons built by the proof. It starts no device and never reads the live commons.

out: every ticket record: ticket A repairs them

measured.saw: build_inspector.derived_successor/continued_successor over the 49 owner and watchme dead paths: 12 agree with the census successor; 23 inference_domain owners get no answer (git saw f942's charter as a delete plus an add: 60e1dd170 --stat shows inference_domain/intention+why.json -62 and inferenceproxy/intention+why.json +63, not a rename); 1 is git-only (orient); 13 owners and 29 watchme paths have no successor. f942a413f26d's plan carries no forwarding order.
measured.how: ran the successor door in-process, read-only, on akienyoga9i against cairn main

measured.saw: the 6 retirements: counting_block and post_commit by 6935a4a71f93 (f2b0d8105); ruling by 640a7a48e1c5 (95ae4ef7a); cairnmap by d547b4859f9a (3882dac1c); liveness by 6208d0a27d6e (b514f6a5f), all 2026-11-08; hermes has no deleting commit in this repo's git log

collision check: 0 of the 3 commons origin branches touch any of the 37 ticket files in bounds.in. 10 or more cairn origin branches touch cairn/machines/build_inspector/ (149b, 0c2c, 7ea5, 17d5, 2711, 39ec, c058, 1244, a4a3, akien-cc-design-boundary)
measured.how: git diff --name-only origin/main...<branch> over every origin branch in both repos

measured.saw: the readers that throw: cross.charter_dir (cairn/tools/base/cross.py:51), clearance/gate.py:67, and ticket_inspector.owning_intention_resolves (inspector.py:246, which reports and does not throw); ticket_inspector runs only from the watch probe the_corpus_gets_cleaner
measured.how: grep for owning_intention resolvers over cairn/, excluding proofs

how: D1 adds the sieve charter_removal_repoints_its_owners to build_inspector's crossing sieves: git diff --name-status over the build's range, D and R entries for intention+why.json, red for each plan still naming the old path unless rewritten in the range or validly forwarded. D2 is one red-first proof in a scratch repo plus commons, one tooth per clause. Sibling of the records repair (cast-inputs/every-tickets-owning-intention-names-a-charter-that-stands.shaped-plan.json). Sequencing: built now on a branch off main; expect a rebase of inspector.py at land, since 10 or more open branches touch it.
